items.title: EXPOSED: Is AI Safety Dead? OpenAI's Safety Lead Quit and Called Culture Broken

items.title: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN, and IBM simulate 12,635-atom protein complex
items.summary: It can take more than a decade for a medical discovery to become a drug doctors can prescribe. Researchers from @Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM are exploring how hybrid quantum-classical workflows could help accelerate this timeline–with exciting results. Earlier this year, the collaboration successfully simulated the chemistry of two protein complexes with binding agents, T4-Lysozyme and Trypsin. The largest simulation of a Trypsin complex reached 12,635 atoms and more than 30,000 orbitals, earning the milestone of largest heterogeneous quantum-classical (HQC) electronic-structure calculation to date: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Recently nominated as a 2026 Gordon Bell finalist (https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/gordon-bell-finalists-2026), the work showed an improvement in accuracy by 210x within a key step of the workflow over previous approaches, attained through new algorithm developments and the close integration of QPUs, CPUs and GPUs. In the latest entry of our research spotlight series, Dr. Kennie Merz. and Dr. Lara Jehi from Cleveland Clinic join IBM Quantum Head of Applied Quantum Science - Sarah Sheldon to explain how this deep integration of computing paradigms, known as quantum-centric supercomputing, helped achieve this remarkable moment in chemistry simulation at scale.

items.title: Workslop Costs a 10K Firm $9M a Year (with Jeff Hancock and Kate Niederhoffer)
items.summary: #workslop #aiatwork #aiproductivity In Episode #1033, Prof. Jeff Hancock (Professor of Communication at Stanford) and Dr. Kate Niederhoffer (Chief Scientist at BetterUp) join Jon Krohn to explain the hidden cost of AI-generated work. items.title: Jev AI vs Open Source: Can GLiNER Replace It?
items.summary: Jev is one of the most hyped AI models of the year, and it isn't an LLM. TypeSafe's "System One" model doesn't generate text. It makes typed, calibrated decisions in ~90ms. In this video we cover what Jev is and how its API works. We look at why calibrated probability is the real unlock, where Jev fits next to LLMs (and where it doesn't), and the open-source "OpenJev" alternatives you can run on your own machine. Finally, we think fast and slow, pairing a System One model with an LLM coach to beat solo Jev at Doom. 📌 Full article with benchmarks, charts and methodology: https://jamesbriggs.io/understanding-jev What we found: - Calibration: Jev's confidence means something. ECE 0.053 vs 0.119 for gpt-5.6-luna on CLINC150. - Speed: ~90ms per call on the server vs ~700ms for gpt-5.6-luna with no reasoning. Extra questions in the same call add no latency. - Accuracy: Jev matches or beats gpt-5.6-luna on 5 of 6 intent, tool-selection and guardrail benchmarks. - Open source: GLiNER2.5 and GLiGuard run in 10–50ms on an M4 Pro Mac and come close on several benchmarks. They don't match Jev's calibration yet. - Fast + slow: adding an LLM coach to Jev and GLiNER gives ~4x their solo Doom deathmatch scores. ⏱️ Chapters 0:00 Intro 1:22 What is JEV? 2:40 Inputs and outputs 4:26 Three types of decision 6:35 Calibrated probability 10:38 Ultra-fast 11:44 Where JEV fits 14:58 Closed source 16:39 Open-source alternatives 20:28 GLiNER 23:33 The trade-offs 25:42 Thinking fast and slow 31:30 What to make of JEV 👋 Find me X: https://x.com/jamescalam LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamescalam/ GitHub: https://github.com/jamescalam #AI #LLM #AIAgents
items.summary_html:
Jev is one of the most hyped AI models of the year, and it isn't an LLM. TypeSafe's "System One" model doesn't generate text. It makes typed, calibrated decisions in ~90ms.

In this video we cover what Jev is and how its API works. We look at why calibrated probability is the real unlock, where Jev fits next to LLMs (and where it doesn't), and the open-source "OpenJev" alternatives you can run on your own machine. Finally, we think fast and slow, pairing a System One model with an LLM coach to beat solo Jev at Doom.

📌 Full article with benchmarks, charts and methodology:
https://jamesbriggs.io/understanding-jev

What we found:
- Calibration: Jev's confidence means something. ECE 0.053 vs 0.119 for gpt-5.6-luna on CLINC150.
- Speed: ~90ms per call on the server vs ~700ms for gpt-5.6-luna with no reasoning. Extra questions in the same call add no latency.
- Accuracy: Jev matches or beats gpt-5.6-luna on 5 of 6 intent, tool-selection and guardrail benchmarks.
- Open source: GLiNER2.5 and GLiGuard run in 10–50ms on an M4 Pro Mac and come close on several benchmarks. They don't match Jev's calibration yet.
- Fast + slow: adding an LLM coach to Jev and GLiNER gives ~4x their solo Doom deathmatch scores.

items.title: CoreWeave Forge: Demo from Fully Connected 2026, with Corey Sanders
items.summary: The complete CoreWeave Forge demo from Fully Connected 2026: Corey Sanders takes a help desk agent through the whole AI loop, uncut. Start building on CoreWeave Forge: https://www.coreweave.com/forge What you're watching: Corey's IT help desk agent files tickets, sets a priority, and routes them, and sometimes it gets the priority or the routing wrong. Over eleven minutes he fixes it without leaving Forge: he instruments the app, finds the failing pattern in production, picks a fix with ARIA, trains with serverless reinforcement learning, proves the new version wins, and ships it with its history attached.
